hero_deck: Lima's airport had never charged international transfer passengers a fee. I designed the web channel to collect it, one of four ways to pay, and handed it over.
hero_role1: Roles — Internal consultant · UX/UI designer · Planning coordinator
hero_role3: Scope — Planning → UX/UI design → prototyping → evaluation → handoff
hero_rv_txt: A passenger lands in Lima and connects to another international flight. At the new terminal they owe a fee the airport had never charged, and no channel existed to collect it. Five areas each held a piece of the problem. As the internal consultant from Processes and Innovation, I coordinated the planning between them, designed the web payment flow, evaluated it and handed it to the team that built it. TUUA Transfer runs today, charging 130,000+ international transfer passengers a month.
act3_verdict: A fee the airport had never charged, through a channel that did not exist. I designed the channel and handed it over.
act3_scan1: TUUA Transfer is a charge on international-transfer passengers at Jorge Chávez and a new line of airport revenue. It runs today against more than 130,000 of them a month.
act3_scan2: Five divisions each held a piece of it — Finanzas, Operaciones Aeroportuarias, TI, Comercial and Reputación — and engineering was waiting on a definition.
act3_scan3: My deliverables closed on 4 August 2025, and the closure mail lists them: technical scopes for the platform and for the payment gateway, the screen mockup and web prototype, the operational casuistry estimating web-payment usage, and the process map — a blueprint for the physical payment points and a flowchart for the web one.
act3_c1_x: Stakeholder review sessions for the digital platform, and field observation at the physical payment booths, evidenced by two pre-trial surveys and a set of qualitative notes. They are different methods answering different questions, and neither stands in for the other.
act3_c2_x: The same closure mail states that development would add one to two screens beyond the ones I proposed, with minor adjustments, gated on Billing's approval of the final version. The line between my deliverable and the vendor's is written into the programme's own documents, not only into my account of it.
act3_c3_t: What the charter says about me
act3_c3_x: The programme charter's stakeholder table does not list me as its owner. That is the accurate record and this page keeps it.
act3_cp_eyebrow: A year later, I walked the live platform against my own proposal
act3_cp_verdict: The platform is live, it is not mine, and the difference between what I proposed and what shipped is public.
act3_cp_method: Public, unauthenticated pages only. No transaction was submitted, no session was captured, and no data was collected beyond what any visitor sees.
act3_cp_scan1: Four screens are reachable before the payment control itself: the homepage, an eligibility self-declaration, a flight-details screen carrying the fee, and a customer-details screen. The pass stops there, deliberately, one control short of paying.
act3_cp_scan2: Personal-data capture was not removed from my proposal — it was reordered to follow the flight lookup rather than precede it, and I measured it doing exactly that on the customer-details screen. I read the reordering as intuitive and do not contest it.
act3_cp_scan3: The fee is settled at $11.86, shown a full screen earlier than I proposed, and consistent between its two appearances — $23.72 for two passengers. Fee-setting was never my decision, so the live figure is the correct reference rather than a delta against the $11.32 in my mockup.
act3_cp_scan4: Eligibility is gated by a self-declaration click — "Soy ese tipo de pasajero" — rather than the automatic agreement check the technical scope specified. To my own knowledge of the build, that check was never implemented as written. This pass could not see past its own boundary to confirm it.
act3_cp_findings: Six findings: one major, five minor, none critical. The major one is a screen headed "Ingresa tus datos personales y de tu vuelo" whose only fields are flight data.
act3_cp_synth: I can read the gap between proposal and build in public, which is a better position than having to describe it.
act3_notice: TUUA Transfer. I understand the platform's mechanism and contributed to its UX/UI design — not its development, deployment or operation.
